messages.author: 4ed22e91e8ca0bf6
messages.subject: Mollweide projection
parts:
Hi folks,

I am wondering if there is a way to render a Mollweide projection in
ggplot.
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollweide_projection
I have a data frame of different galactic latitudes and longitudes
that I want to be able to map.

~Nitish Chopra

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Mollweide projection
parts:
hi,

try using:

coord_map(project="mollweide")

see ?mapproject that is used internally in coord_map.
--

messages.author: 1f7d7be0d66dbecf
messages.subject: Funky behavior from ggplot2 with geom_text
parts:
Hi.

Using this code, ggplot2 overwrites the contents of the legend when the geom_text argument to "size" > 3.

dev.new()
p = ggplot(data=Z, aes(x=Longitude,y=Latitude, group=Source, shape=Source, colour=Source)) 
p = p + geom_point() + scale_colour_hue(name="Source") + scale_shape_discrete(name="Source")
p + geom_text(aes(label=CommonName),hjust=0.2,size=3) 

I used size=10 just to illustrate; < 4 the legend is unadulterated.  Haven't tried floats, just integers.
Thanks for any help.

Cheers.
--------------

messages.subject: Re: Funky behavior from ggplot2 with geom_text
parts:
John, 

I ran your code and I'm not sure what you mean. Is your problem that the size of the text overwrites the shapes? I'm not sure there is a way around that, unless you split the legend into two? 

If you only want the points you could do legend=FALSE in your geom_text() [or vice versa with the geom_point()].

Brandon

messages.author: 92a06be4d96a96ee
messages.subject: Re: Funky behavior from ggplot2 with geom_text
parts:
That's my standard solution!  I'll often make a dummy data.frame so my legend can be points and the graph only text. 

if your data is in a data.frame df:

dummy<-df[1,]
dummy[,2]<-NaN

ggplot()+geom_text(data=df,
aes(...),legend=F)+geom_point(data=dummy,aes(...),na.rm=T)

John, 

I ran your code and I'm not sure what you mean. Is your problem that the size of the text overwrites the shapes? I'm not sure there is a way around that, unless you split the legend into two? 

If you only want the points you could do legend=FALSE in your geom_text() [or vice versa with the geom_point()].

Brandon
